missing_algorithms: No gradual rollout / canary percentage algorithm for feature flags — _get_features returns a static list with no rollout percentage, no user-bucketing, no experimentation framework
No backward-compatibility or migration algorithm for onboarding state when tiers change — no versioned state schema, no upgrade path when a user's tier is re-evaluated
No heuristic or ML-based tier refinement — no feedback loop to adjust scoring weights or thresholds based on actual usage patterns or outcomes
No recommendation explanation algorithm — recommend_tier_scored returns a bare string with no reasoning trace, confidence score, or alternative-tier suggestions
No per-module completion estimation algorithm — no time/cost/complexity scoring per module to help users plan their onboarding effort
No runtime dependency resolution — ModuleDependencyGraph computes install order but no algorithm resolves conflicts when a user skips a prerequisite or installs modules out of order
No health-check or readiness-probe algorithm — no post-install verification that a module is actually functional (e.g., DB reachable, API responding, sensor data flowing)
No external-service dependency declaration — no algorithm to check that required infrastructure (PostgreSQL, Redis, object store, message queue) is available before module installation begins
bottlenecks: ModuleRegistry uses a static dict — adding a tier or module requires editing source code; no plugin/registry extension point or config-driven module list
No caching of tier lookups or module lists; repeated calls rebuild data (trivial now, becomes real with dynamic registries or remote config)
Flat module list with no lazy loading — all modules for a tier are always returned even if the user only needs a subset
No async/concurrent module initialization — onboarding wizard would block on each module setup sequentially
test_all_recommended_modules_importable only asserts module_name.isidentifier() — it is a name-shape check, not an actual import or smoke test; gives false confidence
No onboarding state persistence — wizard state lives only in memory; a session restart loses all progress with no way to resume
No onboarding API — no REST/gRPC endpoints for programmatic access to tier recommendation, module listing, or setup status
No onboarding CLI — no `agtech onboard init` / `agtech onboard status` / `agtech onboard validate` command for headless or CI/CD onboarding
No metrics or telemetry — no instrumentation to track onboarding completion rates, drop-off points, or module setup duration
No rollback or undo mechanism for completed onboarding steps — once a module is marked complete there is no way to revert
No notification/reminder system for incomplete onboarding steps — no email, webhook, or in-app nudge when onboarding stalls
No integration with identity providers (SSO, OAuth) for enterprise onboarding — no automated provisioning of users/roles
No data import/migration tooling for existing farms transitioning into the platform — no CSV/JSON bulk import for fields, sensors, or historical data
benchmark_gaps: No feature-flag runtime control — _get_features returns a compile-time list; no way to toggle features without redeploying, no per-environment or per-tenant overrides
No A/B testing framework for onboarding variants — no way to experiment with different wizard flows, scoring weights, or template configs
No multi-language or accessibility support in onboarding flow — all strings are hard-coded English, no i18n, no screen-reader or keyboard-nav considerations
No onboarding analytics dashboard — no visualization of funnel conversion, time-to-complete, or module-level drop-off
No integration with external monitoring/observability — no OpenTelemetry spans, no structured logging of onboarding events for debugging
No support for partial or incremental onboarding — wizard is all-or-nothing; no way to complete a subset of modules and defer the rest
No dry-run or preview mode — users cannot see what a tier's setup will produce (config diff, module list, cost estimate) before committing
No cost estimation or resource planning — no algorithm to estimate infrastructure cost (compute, storage, bandwidth) based on tier and scale inputs
